original_title: After a 'corporate mandate' demanded they help with Call of Duty, Toys for Bob studio head says it took 'many mini miracles' to buy their independence from Activision
summary_en: The beloved studio behind Spyro and Crash Bandicoot has officially announced its return to independence. This move comes after a period of forced work on Call of Duty titles.
ai_analysis: Toys for Bob's journey back to independence highlights the creative tension between studio passion and corporate directives in the modern gaming landscape.

en.title: Toys for Bob Buys Back Independence After Call of Duty Mandate
en.summary: The beloved studio behind Spyro and Crash Bandicoot has officially announced its return to independence. This move comes after a period of forced work on Call of Duty titles.
en.body:
After a tumultuous period that saw them shift focus away from beloved franchises, **Toys for Bob** has officially announced its successful bid to regain independence from Microsoft. The studio, renowned for its work on the **Spyro Reignited Trilogy** and **Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time**, revealed its new independent status at the recent Xbox Games Showcase, much to the delight of its passionate fanbase.

This significant development follows a challenging few years for the development team. In 2021, **Toys for Bob** was reportedly shifted to a support role for Activision's massive franchises, primarily **Call of Duty: Warzone** and **Overwatch 2**, a decision that studio head Paul Yan described as a "corporate mandate." While the studio took pride in its contributions to these titles, Yan candidly admitted that "deep down inside, we knew that it wasn't the right fit. And we were getting away from the types of games that we love to make and we're best known for doing."

## The Road to Independence

The desire to return to their roots and create original experiences solidified during the period leading up to Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard. The impending changes brought about by the acquisition provided the impetus for **Toys for Bob** to "double down and bet on ourselves in a big way," proposing a "radical" plan to buy back their independence. This negotiation, described by Yan as requiring "many mini miracles," ultimately paved the way for the studio's liberation and its ability to once again pursue its own creative vision. The studio's history, which includes creating the **Skylanders** franchise and revitalizing classics like **Spyro** and **Crash Bandicoot**, underscores their talent for crafting unique and engaging gameplay experiences.

## What This Means for Fans

For fans eagerly awaiting new adventures from the **Toys for Bob** team, this news is a monumental victory. The studio's dedication to its own IP and its proven track record with beloved characters mean that the future looks bright for original game development. While the exact nature of their upcoming projects remains under wraps, the announcement at the Xbox Games Showcase, coupled with the return to independence, signals a renewed focus on the kind of innovative and joyful gaming experiences that **Toys for Bob** is celebrated for. The community has long hoped for the studio to once again lead development on its own franchises, and this independence is a crucial step in that direction.

## What's Next

While specific project details are still emerging, **Toys for Bob** has confirmed that they are actively working on new, original titles. Fans can anticipate further announcements regarding their future endeavors as the studio embarks on this exciting new chapter. The studio continues to support **Crash Bandicoot** titles, and has also been involved with **Call of Duty**, but their newfound independence allows them to chart their own course.

tr.title: Toys for Bob, Özgürlüğe Geri Dönüyor: Call of Duty'ün Getirdiği Yükten Kurtuldular
tr.summary: Toys for Bob, beloved oyun stüdyosunun, uzun süredir beklenen bir gelişme ile bağımsız bir şekilde çalışmaya geri döndüğü açıklandı. Bu gelişme, stüdyonun Call of Duty serileri için çalışmaya zorlandığı bir dönemin ardından geldi.
tr.body:
Toys for Bob, Spyro ve Crash Bandicoot serilerinin yeniden canlandırılmasında önemli bir rol üstlenen stüdyo, Microsoft'un kontrolünden bağımsız olarak çalışmaya geri dönmüş durumda. Bu gelişme, stüdyonun yeni bağımsız statüsünü açıklamasıyla geldi ve hayranlar da bu haberden büyük bir memnuniyet duydu.

Bu önemli gelişme, stüdyonun son birkaç yılını zorlayan bir döneme denk geldi. 2021 yılında, Toys for Bob, Activision'un devasa franchise'lerine destek olarak çalışmaya zorlandı. Bu franchise'ler arasında Call of Duty: Warzone ve Overwatch 2 yer alıyordu. Stüdyo başkanı Paul Yan, bu gelişmeyi "işletme emri" olarak tanımlarken, stüdyonun bu projelere katkısını takdir ettiğini ancak "içimizden, doğru bir fit olmadığını biliyorduk" dedi.

## Özgürlüğe Geri Dönüş Yolu

Toys for Bob'un köklerine dönmeye karar vermesinde, Microsoft'un Activision Blizzard'ı satın alması etkili oldu. Bu satın almayla gelen değişimler, stüdyonun "daha da kendimize inanıp kendimize güvenerek" hareket etmesine sebep oldu. Stüdyo, "radikal" bir planla bağımsız olma yolunda ilerledi ve sonunda bu girişimden başarıyla çıktı. Stüdyonun geçmişi, Skylanders serisinin yaratılmasına ve klasik oyunların yenilenmesine tanık oldu. Bu, stüdyonun benzersiz ve etkileyici oyun deneyimleri yaratma yeteneğini kanıtladı.

## Hayranlar için Ne Demektedir?

Toys for Bob'un yeni projelerini bekleyen hayranlar için bu haber, büyük bir zafer. Stüdyonun kendi IP'lerine ve sevilen karakterlere olan bağlılığı, yeni oyun geliştirme için parlak bir geleceğe işaret ediyor. Stüdyonun yeni projelerinin tam detailsi hala gizli olmasına rağmen, Xbox Games Showcase'da yapılan açıklama ve bağımsız olma kararı, stüdyonun yenilikçi ve keyifli oyun deneyimleri yaratma yeteneğini yeniden canlandırdı. Stüdyonun bağımsız olma kararı, uzun süredir beklenen bu gelişme, hayranların stüdyonun kendi franchise'lerini yeniden canlandırmasını beklemesini sağladı.

## Gelecek İçin Ne Var?

Stüdyonun yeni projeleri hakkında henüz tam detailsi belli olmamasına rağmen, Toys for Bob, yeni, özgün oyunlar üzerinde çalışmaya devam ettiğini doğruladı. Hayranlar, stüdyonun gelecekteki girişimlerine dair daha fazla bilgi almak için beklemeye devam edebilirler. Stüdyo, Crash Bandicoot serilerine devam ediyor ve Call of Duty'ye de katkısı var. Ancak bağımsız olma kararı, stüdyonun kendi yollarını çizmesine olanak tanıyor.

content_raw: It's been a bit of a journey for Toys for Bob, the studio behind the very good Spyro: Reignited Trilogy, that's now making its own original Spyro game as an independent studio, as announced at the Xbox Games Showcase . Despite Reignited's smashing success selling over 11 million copies, Toys for Bob was shifted to be a support studio for Call of Duty: Warzone back in 2021, also lending a hand to Overwatch 2. Then, in 2024, Microsoft laid off a whopping 1900 people after acquiring Activision Blizzard , which caught 86 staff from the studio in the crossfire —the very next month, the studio announced it'd be going indie . Now, in a chat with IGN , it's been revealed that Toys for Bob's motivations were… well, about what you'd expect, given that turbulent past: "There was a corporate mandate for us to move and support larger initiatives," says studio head Paul Yan, "Games like Warzone and Overwatch 2. And Toys for Bob stepped up to support those initiatives and support those teams and those games, and we're very proud of the work that we did." However, "deep down inside, we knew that it wasn't the right fit. And we were getting away from the types of games that we love to make and we're best known for doing." That sordid experience with Microsoft crystalised the studio's desire to go independent, though Yan is far more diplomatic about it: "Right around 2023, around that time period, Microsoft was in the position of acquiring Activision … With the amount of change that was on the horizon with the acquisition, and the transition that was coming up, we felt that was the right time for us to say 'let's double down and bet on ourselves in a big way, and let's propose something really radical'. "We put forth a plan that said 'hey, we'd like to buy back our independence and take back creative control, organisational control, financial control, and then spin out as a separate company in order to focus on the kinds of games we love'," and, pointedly, "to preserve the team and all the tenure that we'd built." In an interview with PC Gamer at Summer Game Fest, Yan said that it took "many mini miracles" to achieve the buyout, and affirmed that the studio is in a much happier place making the next great platformer than toiling away in the Call of Duty mines. Personally, I'm, pleased as punch. Spyro was a huge part of my early gaming days—I played the original trilogy back on the PS1 and I was very bad at it, on account of the fact I was around five years old at the time—so for there to be a new Spyro game on the horizon from a studio clearly invested in going back to formula has me hyped. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together
